content.text:
You are fixing a known divergence in the Email OS Gmail worker (called KD-1 in the repo). I coordinate the maintenance programme from thread `c07c9c54-0efc-4c81-81d7-dc1548e15e3c`; I run the full end-to-end gate and merge. You open the PR and do not merge.

## The problem
When Gmail definitely rejects one queued mailbox write, the worker ends its pass in sync-error backoff, so the other queued writes (for example the other members of a group archive) stay `queued` until the next retry tick: about a minute, and up to 10 minutes after repeated failures (`MAX_BACKOFF_INTERVAL` in `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs`). The browser fake drains them immediately. The owner has decided: **the worker should keep draining past a write that was definitely rejected, and keep backing off when the account or the network is the problem.**

## Where it is
- `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/operations.rs`, `run_one`. It already separates the cases:
  - transient or account-wide errors (`NetworkUnavailable`, `ProviderUnavailable`, `InvalidProviderResponse`, `RateLimited`, `AuthRequired`, `PermissionRequired`, `SecretsUnavailable`) requeue the operation and return `Err`. **Keep this: stop and back off.**
  - the catch-all arm calls `store.fail_operation` and then also returns `Err`. This is the definite, operation-scoped rejection. **This is the one to change**, so the pass continues to the next queued write.
  - `StorageUnavailable` halts. Keep.
  - the account-mismatch branch (`profile.account_id != record.account_id`) is account-wide. Keep it stopping.
- `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs` around the `PassAction::Mutations` branch turns `run_one`'s result into `PassOutcome::{Complete, Idle, SyncError, Halt, Cancelled}`.
- `crates/mail-core/tests/contract_scenarios.rs`: `KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` has two KD-1 entries (profiles `gmail` and `synthetic`) for scenario `group-member-failure-does-not-stop-siblings`. The runner requires listed scenarios to fail, so both entries must go once this works.
- `sync.rs` test `synthetic_tick_rearms_queued_writes_after_a_definite_failure` asserts the old behaviour (sibling stays `Queued` until the tick).

## What I need you to decide and show
Read the code before choosing the shape of the change. I think the smallest correct change is for the definite-rejection arm to finish as a completed pass, but check these and say what you found:
1. What does the user lose if that failure no longer becomes a `SyncError`? The failed operation must still show as failed with its error and stay retryable from Activity. If the account status line currently relies on the `SyncError` to tell the user anything they would otherwise miss, say so and keep that information reachable.
2. Backoff state: a completed pass resets `st.backoff`. Is it right that a definite rejection, which proves the provider answered, clears backoff built up by earlier transient failures? Decide and justify in the PR.
3. Uncertain-outcome reconciliation (`reconcile`, `finish_unlanded`) has its own failure paths. Do not change them unless the same stall exists there; if it does, report it instead of widening this PR.
4. Which errors actually reach the catch-all arm today? List them in the PR so the owner can see nothing account-wide is hiding there. If one of them is really account-wide, move it to the stop-and-back-off arm.

## Tests (write the failing ones first)
- Definite rejection of the first of two queued writes: the second is `Confirmed` without any tick, for both the `gmail` and `synthetic` profiles.
- Transient failure of the first: the second stays `Queued` and the pass ends in backoff (the behaviour that must not change).
- The review finding behind `synthetic_tick_rearms_queued_writes_after_a_definite_failure` was "with discovery off, the periodic tick must still re-arm queued writes". That property still matters after a transient failure. Keep a test for it, driven by a transient failure, if the synthetic provider or the shared fake can inject one; if neither can, say so rather than dropping the coverage silently.
- Remove both `KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` entries; the contract scenario must now pass on both Rust profiles.

## Docs
Update what describes KD-1 as current behaviour: `docs/development.md` (the "today only KD-1" sentence), `docs/current-architecture.md` if it names it, and any other mention you find by searching for `KD-1` and "definite failure".

## Tell the owner the cost
In the PR description, state plainly: if Gmail rejects every write, the queue now fails one by one without pausing; each failed write stays retryable from Activity.

## Rules
- Share the cargo target: `export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target`. Run one heavy command at a time. The shared target can serve stale results from other checkouts: `touch crates/mail-core/src/lib.rs src-tauri/src/lib.rs src-tauri/src/main.rs` before lint, and `touch crates/mail-core/src/bin/generate-types.rs crates/mail-core/src/lib.rs` before `mise run check:contract`.
- Before the PR: `mise run check:all` green. Report test counts (main today: mail-core 366, native 18, frontend 1,888 in 104 files).
- No wire-contract change is expected. If `check:contract` shows a diff after the touch above, stop and tell me.
- Privacy rule: never log subjects, addresses, bodies, tokens, URLs with ids, or SQL with bound values.
- Synthetic fixtures only. No real accounts, credentials or Google network.
- Never touch the root checkout `/home/exedev/email-os` except `git fetch`. Work in your worktree.
- PR to `main` on `BbrSofiane/email-os` (the remote is a proxy URL: pass `-R BbrSofiane/email-os` to `gh`). Commit at checkpoints so nothing is lost if you are cut off.

## Report
End with: the shape you chose and why, answers to the four questions above, tests added or changed, test counts, anything not verified, and the PR URL.
I'll start by reading the code.
